newsitem.title: CANADA: Teens who escaped cult suicide leave for France.
newsitem.headline: Teens who escaped cult suicide leave for France.

text.p: Three teenagers who escaped a group suicide of members of the Solar Temple death cult have left for France, Quebec officials said on Tuesday.
"The teenagers are in France for good with their family. They left Quebec City on Sunday," Quebec Youth Protection Agency spokesperson Jean Lortie told Reuters.

Fanny, Julien and Tom Queze, aged 13 to 16, left Canada just two weeks after authorities decided not to charge them in the death of their parents Didier Queze and Chantale Goupillot, found burned to death near Quebec City on March 22.
Goupillot's mother, Suzanne Druau, and two friends of the Queze couple, Bruno Klaus and Pauline Rioux, were also found dead.
The children, who were born and raised in Quebec, were visited by relatives from Europe after the incident.
Quebec authorities said they made sure the relatives, who are said to be the grandparents of the three teens, had no links with the Order of the Solar Temple.
The Solar Temple is an international doomsday cult whose members believe a ritualized death takes them on a journey to a new life on the star Sirius.

Since 1994, 74 cult members and others haved been killed in group suicides and murders in Quebec, France and Switzerland. Some of the victims, including children and infants, were shot, poisoned, stabbed or asphyxiated with plastic bags.
